name: Saturday Slam #68

date.source: The show's own dateline in each of its posted parts ("1.17.98") and the fed's weekly Saturday Slam numbering.

no_appearances_reason: A dozen-plus named wrestlers, a two-man commentary team, a ring announcer and a referee appear across three matches, but the fed's own wider 1998 run and its own title lineages were not read into shards; registering some names now would leave a visibly partial roster.
notes: The fed's own weekly televised card, posted in four parts (a disclaimer plus two hours and an overrun segment) and reassembled here as one document.

name: Saturday Slam #69

date.source: The show's own dateline in each of its posted parts ("1.24.98") and the fed's weekly Saturday Slam numbering.

no_appearances_reason: Multiple named wrestlers appear across several matches and interview segments, but the fed's own wider 1998 run and its own title lineages were not read into shards; registering some names now would leave a visibly partial roster.
notes: The fed's own weekly televised card, posted in three parts (two hours plus an overrun segment) and reassembled here as one document.

name: Saturday Slam #75

date.source: The show's own dateline ("3.28.98") and the fed's weekly Saturday Slam numbering.

no_appearances_reason: A large named roster and a cross-promotional angle with a rival federation's own on-air figure appear across this long card, but the fed's own wider 1998 run and its own title lineages were not read into shards; registering some names now would leave a visibly partial roster.
notes: The fed's own weekly televised card, posted whole in one part.

name: May Madness 98

date.source: The show's own dateline ("5.25.98") and its own on-air billing as "MLWO May Madness 1998", staged from the fed's own arena in Baltimore, Maryland.

no_appearances_reason: An eight-match pay-per-view card with a large named roster, including a cage main event for a vacant world title, but the fed's own wider 1998 run and its own title lineages were not read into shards; registering some names now would leave a visibly partial roster.
notes: The fed's own May pay-per-view, posted in three parts (three hours) and reassembled here as one document.

name: Wednesday Washout

date.source: The post's own subject, "Wednesday Washout 11/06/96", read as month, day and year, and its opening Washout the day after Battle Bowl.

matches.note: Style wins with a DDT after kicking Dragon low; a taped Johnny Razorblade jeer and a jumping of Style by ER and Razorblade follow.
Billed as the Industrial Revolution against a mystery team; the opponent is Steve Sampson alone, who wins with the Japanese Armbar when MegaDiesel gives up.
Latini's debut: a German suplex, a slingshot facebuster and the LatiniPlex, two minutes in.
Adams and Martin win with the Hollywood Wrapup after a golden beer can, the "six pack of whoopass", is handed to Adams.
North American Tag Team Championship: Terminator's Death Drop wins it from Da Ghetto Blasters; the page calls them new champions.
United States Championship: Patrinne, champion, keeps it with a flying somersault headbutt after Venom's Injection misses; his father Vic is at ringside.
North American Championship: Mongol wins it with a flying bulldog and the page calls him the new champion.

notes: The VPWF's Wednesday show, posted as the fed formerly the MLWO. Seven matches are announced and worked; three are title matches (North American Tag, United States, North American) and two change hands. The page opens with a French-language promo and three dressing-room scenes, and closes with a live interview that ends in an attack and a Slam update.

name: Battle Bowl

date.source: The roster post of 4 November 1996 bills "Battle Bowl, a special impromptu card tomorrow", and the poster says it was mailed on the Tuesday, 5 November; the Wednesday Washout of 6 November opens with "yesterday's victor".

matches.note: First round: Renge pins with a double flip shooting star press after Kanemoto canes Atkins.
First round: Clark's springboard headscissors into a cradle wins it after Reece low-blows Rivers.
First round: Patrinne snaps, brawls with MacDuffy and clocks his own partner; Dark Master wins with a DDT.
First round: LaChance pulls Mauler off a slingshot splash and pins Venom after a flying clothesline.
First round: Adams chair-shots Tuf and Gravedigger and puts Mongol out with a sleeper.
First round: after a Diamond Cutter on Sampson, Martin German-suplexes Jeffries for the pin.
First round: a thirteen-second match; Derrick Steele chairs everyone and Spot superbombs Jayrock for the pin.
First round: a Diamond Cutter by Cheese on Style wins it as the lights go out and a voice claims to be Mutilator.
Second round: Martin trips his own partner and chairs Cheese; LaChance pins with a German suplex.
Second round: Adams' Rock forces the submission after a fire extinguisher and brass knuckles.
Second round: Vic Patrinne stops Steele from winning, and Reaper rolls Steele up for the pin after a long, brutal match.
Second round: Rex pins Spot with a small package.
Semifinal: a squash; Legend wins with the Legend Plex after thirty seconds.
Semifinal: Adams pins Dark Master after LaChance's Northern Lights superplex and a piledriver through a table.
Final: Adams canes everyone but LaChance at Vic's orders and piledrives Legend on the cane; LaChance hits the Bite a ti-Guy and pins Legend.

matches.stipulation: Three-way, shot at the World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Renge is eliminated first by Van Dam's pin; LaChance then counters a Northern Lights suplex into the Bite a ti-Guy and pins Van Dam for the title shot against Mauler on 16 November.

notes: An impromptu card built as a six-man elimination tournament. Three names are drawn from a hat for each side; sixteen matches run through five first-round pairings, four second-round, two semifinals and a final, the last a three-way for a shot at the World Champion, Mauler, on 16 November. Vic Patrinne and Mark Cutter draw the names; Vic announces a ban on the letters MLWO.

name: Saturday SLAM: The Hype

date.source: The announcer's own opening: "VPWF Saturday SLAM, The Hype, on December 14, 1996."

matches.note: A victory roll beats Bash after his extra-impact Superbomb gets two; Tyler Steele is with Bash.
Billed as the King of Dogs; Mutilator wins with the Armpit Claw, then breaks up Violence Unlimited on the mic.
A Quantum Kick ends it; Bash is with Steele.
Mutilator chairs Steele and applies the Armpit Claw before the bell; Legend lets Mutilator go and wins when the referee stops it.
Tiff trips Venom and Patrinne DDTs him and pins him.
North American Tag Team Championship: ER retain after Saunders drops from the rafters in an accidental moonsault on MegaDiesel.
Billed as Shaolin's Finest against the Colossals; Young pins Powerhouse with the Young Gun after a bed of thumbtacks is used on all four.
Renge, the HardCore champion, rolls Sampson up while Vic Patrinne talks over the match from the booth.
World Tag Team Titles: Reaper falls off the railing after a springboard attempt, Dark Master slips, and Punk covers; Da Ghetto Blasters keep the belts.
Non-title. Mongol, back from Japan and arrested the night before, wins after a shovel handle across Martin's throat; the page says the charges are dropped.

notes: The Saturday card three months after the September takeover. The page opens with Guy LaChance's French-language promo, ER and Razorblade promos and an LOD segment, then runs nine matches and a main-event Texas Death Weapons Match between Jim Mongol and Jak Martin, with a flashback to the takeover and Vic Patrinne's booth interview. It closes with the booking of a 64-man tournament over 18 to 31 December and an eighteen-item pay-per-view card.

name: Battle Brawl II

date.source: The post is dated Thursday 30 January 1997 and the show is Thursday Night Titans; its own text gives no date but speaks of February Fallout on the 15th as ahead.

matches.note: Mini World Title: Jakito Martin keeps it with the Hollywood Wrapup.
Torrington takes fall one with a leaping DDT, Pi fall two with a cross body, and Torrington the match with the Dreamer. Wrath attacks Pi afterward.
Mongol misses a plancha to the floor and Reece rolls back in; the page marks the finish (CO).
Pain and Suffering beat the Two Dudes With Attitude with the Hammer Drill.
The Cartel interferes while Tiff distracts the referee; Razorblade wins with the Postage Due Stamp.

A twenty-man battle royal, a new man every two minutes, eliminated by going over the top rope; the winner draws a number between 25 and 35 in the February Fallout match. Eliminated in the order the page marks them: Ultimate Mark, Mike Jeffries, The Crow, Chris Deugau, Andy Saunders, Scott Paulson, J-Dog, Stone, Mick Morton, Steve Latini, Marcus Renge, Phoenix, Danny Style, Steve Sampson, Eric Sampson and Dark Master; Jak Martin then throws out Damien Legend, and Martin and Shawn Adams go over together as Guy LaChance falls from the top. The announcer gives the match to Guy LaChance.

notes: The Thursday Night Titans show under the Battle Brawl II banner: five matches and a twenty-man battle royal whose winner draws a number between 25 and 35 in the February Fallout match. The page opens with promos (Justin B on Damien Legend's family home, Pi on Torrington, Razorblade on Tommy Van Dam, the LOD), a chat transcript with the Danger Zone Alliance, a Barry Hart arrival, and ends with highlights of a PCW Birthday Brawl, the Slam card and the February Fallout lineup.

name: Thursday Night Titans

date.source: The post's own subject, "Thursday Night Titans {2/6/97}".

matches.note: A squash: a baseball bat clothesline.
Simply Anhiliation's debut, with Sunny B; Lucifer gives up to the Nanimo Cloverleaf.
A dark match, told by the Rednecks Jim Bob and Hoss rather than shown.
A dark match, told by the Rednecks, who say Phoenix (the Dark Destroyer under make-up) won.
Round two, with Bermuda with Pain and Suffering and Pi and Sebrina with the Dudes; Sledge wins with the Hammer Drill from the top of the cage.

notes: Thursday Night Titans of 6 February 1997: a midget debut, a tag debut, two dark matches told by the Rednecks, and a tag team cage match as the main event, with promos by Legend, the LOD, Mongol and Phoenix and the Slam and February Fallout cards.

name: May Madness: The Anniversary

date.source: Part one's own heading: "MLWO MAY MADNESS "The Anniversary" May 25, 1997 Disney World, Buena Vista, FL".

matches.note: Debut match: Scott wins with the Utopian Clawhold and keeps it on after the bell; Dan Kauffman breaks it up.
Debut match: Kauffman wins with the Scorpion Deathlock; a brawl with Super Scott follows and Dark D returns.

matches.stipulation: Disney Death Match: Falls Count Anywhere, Dog Collar
matches.note: Fought through Disney World; N unmasks as Chris North on top of the Magic Kingdom, and Spector pins him on the monorail.
Unified tag titles: the Vegas Fighters defend; Hands of Stone is hurt in a fall from the ladder and the Rednecks win the belts.

Announced winner Matt Harris after fifty-six minutes; the page's closing results line reads "Winner: Caleb Temple" and is left as written. Gryphon and Sydney Smythe interfere against Temple; Jak Martin attacks Temple afterward.

notes: The fed's one-year anniversary pay-per-view, posted in four parts on 6 June 1997 from a card the poster says ran 271K. Part one lists eighteen items; the posted parts carry the Super Scott and Dark Destroyer contract signing, the Jim Goodyear and Dan Kauffman debut matches, the Disney Death Match, the unified tag title ladder match, and Shawn Adams' talk show The Rock with the falls-count-anywhere match. The rest of the card is not posted.

name: Ground Zero

date.source: Part one's own heading: "Convention Center, Ocean City, MD June 28 1997".

matches.note: The Mystery Poet, introduced at 275 pounds, is revealed to be Justin B. ("Mr. Right"). He attacks before the bell, canes Rick Showboat with manager Dr. Love's own cane and wins with the Right Driver.

Network Online Wrestling's match for the NOW World Tag Team Titles, the finals of its six-team tournament, called by Toby James and Rob Scatterson. Craig Anderson eliminates Simply the Best with the Thunderbolt Superplex; Brian Knight then rolls up Dan Kauffman from behind while Kauffman argues with Jennifer Sweet at ringside, and Damage Control, Inc. become the first NOW tag champions. Garrett A. Michaels books the rematch for 19 July at Survival of the Beast.

Time 38:03 as announced. Stevens opens with a metal bat and Dan Kauffman takes it from him; Great Ceasar comes through the crowd and throws a fireball in Gryphon's face; Gryphon has the Spinecracker locked on when Bridget Xavier sprays hair spray in his eyes and Stevens covers him.

Temple charges to the ring with a steel chair, wrecks the draw for the order of entry, claims the first spot and then beats the other seven in turn; Big Cheese throws Temple through the Canadian announcers' table; Snow, at ringside with Steve Phoenix, hits his own man with the chair meant for Temple. After the finish Casey James attacks Temple.

A special challenge. Before it, Jim Russ of the WRF parachutes in with a microphone to present Scott, in a gorilla suit, as the WRF's newest member, and he goes to the ring with him. Russ's interference blinds the Invader and Scott wins with the Utopian Claw. After the bell the Invader pulls hedge clippers from under the ring, hits Scott and unmasks as Imperium; security stops him.

Time 11:31 as announced; the Russian Deathlock. Before the bell Davey Cormier takes the microphone to settle the quarrel behind the match; North takes an early cheap shot and sets a table, and Karelin throws North through it.

United States Championship; Robinson retains. He first ambushes Renge dressed as a janitor with a broomstick, then knocks him out with the hickory stick behind the referee's back, applies the Style and Grace and the referee checks Renge's arm three times. Dan Kauffman then takes the microphone to ask for a title match the next week.

North American Championship, 21 minutes as announced; the title changes hands. Jak Martin brings out the challenger, announced as Steve Sampson and a former MLWO World Heavyweight Champion, and keeps the Militia away from ringside; Dan Kauffman kicks Sampson in the head, and Sampson wins with a sunset flip out of Ice's Militia Drop. The announcers say they will go again the next Saturday.

MLWO World Heavyweight Championship, 34:20 as announced; Martin retains with the Hollywood Wrapup. Harris comes with Danny Ice, Gryphon, Sydney Smythe and the newest Militia member Dan Kauffman; Martin with Steve Sampson, Stone and Miss Tiffany. Caleb Temple appears from under the ring, counts a three for Martin and raises his hand, but the match goes on; Gryphon hits Martin with a chair. After the bell Harris locks on the Agonizer and Sampson clears the ring with a chair.
Billed on the card as a tag team title match, the Rednecks as champions against Shaolin's Finest.

notes: The fed's pay-per-view of 28 June 1997, posted in nine parts on 11 July 1997. The poster's note calls it a tiny filler show, two separate pay-per-views under the Extreme Realization banner after the MLWO chose not to share a joint show with the EWA. Eleven items are billed: the World, United States, North American and tag title matches, an eight-man elimination match, and guest matches from Network Online Wrestling (a tag title triangle) and the GFWA (The Outcast against Randal Lewis III). Vinnie Styles and John Williams call the show with ring announcer Michael Bunker, and Rick Baptist is in charge in the absent president's place. The night runs through a Mystery Poet debut, a Militia and anti-Militia feud, the WRF's Jim Russ and a mystery challenger, and closes on Jak Martin's World Title defence against Matt Harris.

name: Torture Chamber 2

date.source: The posted parts' own subjects, "26 Oct. 97", and part one's banner naming the Tokyo Dome in Tokyo, Japan.

matches.note: The opening match. Vance and Legend double-team Mongol while Matthews holds back from helping; Matthews comes in on the tag, Mongol clears the ring with a double clothesline and beats Vance with a chair, and the part ends on the referee's count of nine over Mongol after Legend breaks a chair over his head.

Called by Tom Olds and Terry Marauder. Hart comes with his bodyguard Slabuu and the weapons come from trash cans around the ring; acting president Owen Curtis, at ringside, talks to the referee to let the match continue and later to get back in and count. Hart wins by pinfall at 41:26 and is booked against Jason Knight for the United States Championship under Softcore rules at the next Saturday Slam.

Called by Rick Baptist and Jack Jenkins. Crane paints EWA over an MLWO flag and Gaines comes with his manager Charlie Chesapeake; a blackout brings a mist and a shadow figure to the turnbuckle, then Paradox, who chairs Crane and stuffs a funeral invitation in his mouth. A silver star descends and Monkeyshine returns, puts Crane's foot on the rope after a Grizzly Slam and whips Gaines down; Crane hits the Jackpot for the pin and the Gaines family runs in.

Called by Hugh Jenner and John Royal; a glove on a fifteen-foot pole, with pinfalls and submissions barred until it is in play. The pole breaks and Jobba goes through the Spanish announce table; Flex retrieves the glove, then staggers into a right hand from Jobba wearing it, and Jobba pins him with the Death Star at 16:35.

matches.stipulation: MLWO World Tag Team Championships, Double Dog Collar Match
matches.note: No disqualification; all four men chained at the neck, with Jobba the Butt at ringside for the champions and Earl Deugau III refereeing. Verhoeven's shooting star press from a ladder puts both Knights through a burning table onto thumbtacks, and the chains are burned off, reattached and tangled together; Hammeneger powerbombs Verhoeven through the guardrail, and Sir Jobs-A-Lot rolls up Kruger out of a powerbomb for the three. The Good Knights retain.

matches.stipulation: MLWO United States Championship, Texas Death Match
matches.note: Called by Vinnie Styles and John Williams, with Paradox's cult at ringside. Knight, who carries a wooden chair and shouts that he does not do hardcore, goes extreme in the aisle; Jim Mongol comes down, holds Paradox for Knight and then powerbombs Knight on the concrete; Paradox pins Knight with the Sweet Sorrow on the steel steps and the ten-count ends the match. Paradox is the new United States Champion.

Pinfalls only, no disqualification, with a steel bullwhip, a baseball bat, a cattle prod and a nightstick hung from the corner poles. Marauder handcuffs a fan before the bell and his father Terry Marauder halts him; Midnight, on a casket, shows a film of his opponent's past. After a false finish at the end of part ten, both men fall from the cage top onto a bed of thumbtacks and Midnight pins Marauder.

matches.stipulation: MLWO World Heavyweight Championship, five-man Torture Cage Match

eliminations.note: Goddess Cutter and a standing moonsault, pinfall
splash through the collapsing cage roof, pinfall
hurricanrana into the Pulse Crusher, pinfall

matches.note: Two rings under one cage, entrants every five minutes through a roof trap door, eliminated men locked in small cages, Jim Smith refereeing; Adams draws number one and Martin, Spector and Harris follow. Harris's cage door sticks until a technician fixes it, and the technician is Renge, who had quit earlier in the night; he goes in with a lead pipe. Renge splashes Spector through the collapsing cage roof for the third elimination and pins Harris with the Pulse Crusher to become World Heavyweight Champion.

notes: The fed's pay-per-view of 26 October 1997 from the Tokyo Dome, posted in twelve parts on 1 November 1997. It opens with Mark Cutter on his hospital bed, then acting president Owen Curtis banning the Dark Destroyer from the building; Cutter walks in with his arm in a cast and is attacked by Barry Hart, who books a Softcore Life match. Ten items are billed: the five-man Torture Cage for the World Heavyweight Championship with the North American Championship to the runner-up, the Armageddon Cage, the Double Dog Collar match for the World Tag Team Championships, the Battle of the Bodyguards, a Texas Death Match for the United States Championship, an EWA non-title match, a Weapons Match, a Texas Tornado tag match, a House of Pain match and an elimination tag match. Vinnie Styles, Mike Wilson and Curt Malone call the show, with Michael Bunker announcing. Barry Hart wins the Weapons Match, Cordell Crane the EWA match after Monkeyshine's return, Jobba the Butt the Coal Miner's Glove match, the Good Knights retain, Paradox takes the United States Title, Captain Midnight wins the Armageddon Cage, and Marcus Renge cuts into the closing cage and wins the World Heavyweight Championship.

name: Saturday Slam

date.source: The post's own opening, "This was a match held on MLWO Saturday Slam earlier today", under its posting date of 11 October 1997 (a Saturday); the post's closing listing of the next Saturday Slam gives the same Kawasaki Stadium in Tokyo, Japan.

matches.note: One fall, decided only by a pin, no time limit. Requiem powerbombs the referee at the first handshake and Otto dominates with head-rams, a backdrop and a missed top-rope splash; a second referee, Jim Smith, is knocked off the cage wall, and the three remaining MLWO referees (Earl Deugau III, Joey Alfonso and Mr. Jones) and a squad of security are put down in turn by chokeslams and Slaughterslams. The two climb the cage wall and fall, brawl through Requiem's Genesis Generation followers, the crowd and the bleachers, and return to the ring, where Otto applies his Meat Cleaver full nelson, dragon suplexes Requiem over the top rope and follows with a plancha. Requiem answers with a top-rope DDT onto a wheelchair and finishes Otto with the Retribution for the three; Nurse Heidi, Otto's wheelchair-bound manager, is at ringside throughout.

notes: The main event of the fed's Saturday Slam of 11 October 1997, reposted to the newsgroup the same day: a no-rules cage match between Requiem, who the announcers say dropped the IIWF World Heavyweight Championship to Brody Thunder the Saturday before, and the former IIWF champion Otto Verhoeven. Vinnie Styles, Mike Wilson and Curt Malone call it, Michael Bunker announces and Panther Tottori referees; the match is billed as not sanctioned by the MLWO. The post closes with the fed's announced cards: a Spotlight on 12 October 1997, Saturday Slam on 19 October 1997 and Torture Chamber 2 on 26 October 1997.

evidence.note: The main event as posted on 11 October 1997.

name: Deadly Games

date.source: Both posts open "Match Originally Broadcast: March 22, 1997" and "Card: MLWO Deadly Games" and give the arena as Madison Square Garden, New York, NY.

matches.note: Team Harris (captain Matt Harris, with Sydney) against Team ICU (captain Exodus; Stone, Deathwatch and Exodus come out with Jak Martin and Miss Tiffany, and the team is billed with a fourth man still unnamed); a double-ring cage, a man from each side in every five minutes with a coin flip for the advantage, a different weapon at each door, and a finish by submission once all are in. Renge opens against Deathwatch, then Ice, Stone, Atkins (drunk), Exodus and Harris, who bursts in with a cheese grater. As the match is about to turn into a rout, Hellshock walks in from the crowd with a chair and a flaming-glove clawhold on Atkins, to a statement for Phoenix; President Mark Cutter says Hellshock is not an MLWO man and the surrender he forced is void. The match resumes and Stone submits to Harris's figure four and Renge's step-down onto a chair across his legs; Team Harris wins. Afterwards Exodus and Deathwatch lock the cage with Harris inside and beat him down until Guy LaChance cuts the cage open with wire cutters and Renge and Ice return.

matches.stipulation: MLWO World Heavyweight Championship, no time limit
matches.note: Mark Cutter takes the commentary seat for the match. Sampson, the challenger, comes with his bodyguard Rick Johnson and his fiancee Adrian Stefani; champion Jak Martin comes with Stone and Miss Tiffany, Stone limping; Jim Smithson referees. A long technical and then brutal match: the referee is knocked out and Stone returns with a chair that he brings down across Sampson's back, Martin hits a superplex and the two trade near-falls past the hour mark. At 1:02:56 Sampson turns Martin's back suplex into a cross body and pins him to become the new MLWO World Heavyweight Champion.

notes: The fed's pay-per-view of 22 March 1997 at Madison Square Garden, known here from two main-event matches that the fed's operator reposted in November 1997 as days one and two of a Year in Review series: the War Games match, called one half of a double main event, and the MLWO World Heavyweight Championship match between Steve Sampson and Jak Martin. The posts do not say which came first, and the rest of the card is not posted; the order below follows the series. Michael Bunker announces.

evidence.note: Day one of the Year in Review series: the War Games match, originally broadcast 22 March 1997.
Day two of the Year in Review series: the World Heavyweight Championship match, originally broadcast 22 March 1997.

name: Slam Supercard 2

date.source: Both posts open "Match Originally Broadcast: April 26, 1997" and "Card: MLWO Slam Supercard 2" and give the arena as the MLWO Arena, Baltimore, MD; the day-three ring announcer calls it "MLWO Saturday Slam...the Supercard number II".

matches.stipulation: MLWO Lightweight Championship, Dog Collar Chain Cage Match
matches.note: Called by Vinnie Styles and Derrick. Spector, in his first dog collar chain match since his apparent death, against Lightweight Champion Matt Harris, who is led to the ring in a noose by Sydney; Harris puts the collar on himself and brawls; the baseball bat and the chain draw blood on both. N drops from the rafters on a bungee cord, lariats both men, locks the collars on their necks, tells Spector he means to send him back to his grave and is attacked by a second Steve Spector who appears; Sydney then puts the noose over Spector's head and she and Harris choke him, and Harris pins him with the Hardcore Driver to keep the title. Harris delivers a speech over the fallen Spector afterwards.

matches.stipulation: MLWO World Heavyweight Championship, steel cage match
matches.note: Fifteen feet of steel with no door; champion Sampson comes alone and challenger Jak Martin, the former champion, comes with Miss Tiffany. Martin's slide kick and plancha take both men outside as the doorless cage is lowered, and they fight there before climbing in; Sampson ties Martin's wrists to the fence and Adrian Stefani splashes him with hot coffee from the crowd. Caleb Temple appears with a wooden cross hung with photographs of Sampson and sets it on fire at the aisle; Stone throws a chair over the cage for Martin. After an hour and thirteen minutes Martin clips the leg and pins Sampson with his legs hooked to become champion for the second time, helps him up and shakes his hand; Temple then chairs Sampson, pours gasoline on him and sets him alight in the shape of a cross, and Martin leaps on him to put the fire out.

notes: The fed's Slam Supercard 2 of 26 April 1997 from the MLWO Arena in Baltimore, Maryland, known from two matches that the fed's operator reposted in November 1997 as days three and four of a Year in Review series: the steel cage rematch for the World Heavyweight Championship, called the main event, and a dog collar chain cage match for the Lightweight Championship. The rest of the card is not posted; the order below puts the posted main event last. Michael Bunker announces.

evidence.note: Day three of the Year in Review series: the World Heavyweight Championship cage match, originally broadcast 26 April 1997.
Day four of the Year in Review series: the Lightweight Championship dog collar chain cage match, originally broadcast 26 April 1997.

name: Winter Inferno 97

date.source: No date is printed in the four posts. The card's video package promises that for one of the eight tournament men "christmas may come ten days early", which puts the night at 15 December 1997 (Christmas Day less ten days); the four parts were posted together on 17 December 1997, a Wednesday.

matches.note: King of Christmas, round two. After promos from both men (Foul renounces his robes and the title Lord Foul to wrestle as The Despiser), the match is called by Randal and Jules. Foul's plancha goes shoulder first into the railing, Heck lands a cane to the head and misses another from the top rope, and Foul breaks a cane over his knee; Alex Adams takes Heck's Soap-on-a-Rope at ringside and Flex Steroidicus bashes Heck with the other cane, and Heck rolls Foul up with the Heck-Plex for the three.

King of Christmas, round two, called by Canada Ken Steigenberger and Trevor Dunn: falls count anywhere and none counts until both men bleed. Stevens comes out with Bridget Xavier and takes a crowbar from a fan; Danny Ice appears on the video wall, says he is tired of beating Stevens and will not come out, and the ring announcer gives the match to Stevens.

King of Christmas, round two, called by Mike Austin and Tony Star on a scaffold about 25 feet above the floor, with no disqualifications. Paradox, the United States Champion, comes with his Cult; Legend pushes the referee into him, the two trade near-falls and near-falls over the edge, and Paradox hits a 450 splash off the scaffold with a chair. Both are out; Legend gets an arm over for the three at 12:12. Justice King then attacks the Cult and Paradox with a chair and barbed wire and promises to bring associates next time.

King of Christmas, round two, called by Rock Barnton and Terry Thunder, with Jack Hampson as a joke ring announcer. Each man is strapped to a leather rope with thumbtacks in it; Deugau files down the tacks, hits the Deugau Death Drop and has his cover broken when Dempsey gets a foot on the ropes. Dempsey comes back with a thrust kick and a leaping move and pins him at 24:33.

Called by Larry Jenkins and Jerry Connors, with The Spunky Lobster as guest ring announcer. Lana Lardcake is first shown in her locker room with Pretty Jimmy, the bodyguard the Rich and Infamous say they hired, dancing for her, and is cut off at the head of the ramp by him. A brawl with chairs, guardrails and the crowd follows; Jobba the Butt watches backstage, smashes a monitor and comes down; Tommy B runs in from the crowd and attacks the Knights. Valor hits Rags to Riches for a near-fall, then holds Sir Jobs-A-Lot in a powerbomb as Hayvin Coules comes off the top rope with a front flip leg drop (3 Story Manslaughter) and covers him for the three: new champions. Tommy B then names the three of them the AKC.

King of Christmas semifinal, called by Jack Cafferty and Leroy Jones for the UEW and the MWF, with a stated twenty-minute limit that the match runs past. The ropes are barbed wire; both men are cut open, Dempsey is tangled in the wire, a Heck-Plex fails because Dempsey is too heavy to lift, and Heck wins with the Heckraiser clothesline from the top rope at 26:57. A video recap of Dempsey's win over Tommy Marauder runs before the match.

King of Christmas semifinal, called by Trevor Dunn and Canada Ken Steigenberger, who shakes his head at the referee and announces the result himself. Stevens, fresh from his forfeit, waits in the ring and will not go outside, for fear of bleeding; Legend is cut on the steel stairs, pulls brass knuckles, which a Stevens dropkick sends into the crowd, and headbutts him in the groin, and a headbutt exchange ends with Legend covering a Stevens whom the commentators dispute is bleeding. Legend is declared the winner and Stevens argues with the referee.

matches.stipulation: Grudge Match, No Disqualification, Torture Cage
matches.note: Called by Mike Wilson and Curt Malone (Vinnie Styles leaves the table when the cage descends); referee Panther Hayoshi, a thirty-minute limit, not sanctioned by the MLWO but counting toward records. Midnight enters from the balcony after a salute of canes from Jim Mongol, Lord Foul, Hoss, Robert Donovan, Steve Spector and Jak Martin and then the crowd. Adams hits Midnight low three times, bends the steel bullwhip across his ribs and has his own eye split open by a cane; Midnight finishes him with the Saint Valentine's Vindicator, a Niagara Driver.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage Match for the World Title shot
matches.note: King of Christmas final, called by Mike Wilson and Curt Malone; head official Jim Smith, no time limit, no disqualifications or countouts, for a shot at the winner of the main event. Heck dominates early with uppercuts and a backbreaker; Legend pulls a chain and brass knuckles, strips a turnbuckle pad so that Heck hits the steel hook, locks the Fantasize sleeper, and wins with a tiger suplex for the three after Heck breaks the sleeper. Legend is named the 1997 King of Christmas.

matches.stipulation: MLWO North American Championship, Two Out of Three Falls Count Anywhere
matches.note: Called by Vinnie Styles, Mike Wilson and Curt Malone. Harris takes the first fall with a spinebuster through the announce table and Spector the second with a jumping DDT on the concrete; in the third Jak Martin runs in with the World Title belt on Spector and piledrives him on the concrete, and Harris ties Spector in his noose in the upper deck, but the noose snaps, both men fall onto a row of seats and Spector lands on top for the third fall and the title. Afterwards Spector offers Harris his respect, then attacks him with three backbreakers, a handspring kneedrop onto a table and a jackknife powerbomb through it. Sydney Smythe watches the pay-per-view from the Harris loft.

matches.stipulation: MLWO World Heavyweight Championship, Ladder Match
matches.note: Main event, called by Vinnie Styles, Mike Wilson and Curt Malone with Mark Cutter at the table; referee Earl Deugau III, no time limit, the belt hung above the ring. The two fight up the ramp and back (a piledriver on the ladder, a swan dive headbutt off the ladder, a Death Valley Driver onto the ladder, ten shots with Robinson's own hickory stick, a swan dive splash through a table and a trade of moonsaults); Alex Adams drops from the roof on a bungee cord and Flex Steroidicus holds the ladder, then they play Martin and Robinson against each other before leaving; Robinson finally climbs to the belt and is named the new champion. Legend, dressed as Santa Claus, hits Robinson with a sack of bricks, takes the belt for himself and tells him to show up on the third to take it back.

notes: The fed's pay-per-view of mid-December 1997 from Madison Square Garden in New York, posted in four parts on 17 December 1997 under the subject [MLWO Winter Inferno 97], with a one-line note from the operator. It was built around the King of Christmas, an eight-man single-elimination tournament with a different stipulation for every match, whose winner earned a shot at the winner of the main event; the posts carry rounds two and three, a Singapore cane match, a Harlem street brawl, a catwalk match and a thumbtack studded strap match, then a barbed wire match and a first blood match as semifinals, and a steel cage final, which "Fantasy" Kevin Legend wins. Around the tournament: the Rich and Infamous take the Unified Tag Team Titles from the Good Knights with Tommy B's help, Captain Midnight beats Alex Adams in a Torture Cage after a cane salute from six wrestlers, Steve Spector takes the North American Championship from Matt Harris two falls to one in a match that goes through the arena, and in the main event Mister Robinson climbs a ladder to take the World Heavyweight Championship from Jak Martin, with Alex Adams and Flex Steroidicus interfering and Legend, dressed as Santa Claus, attacking Robinson afterwards. Vinnie Styles, Mike Wilson and Curt Malone call the show, with Mark Cutter on commentary for the ladder match; other commentary teams and writers call the tournament matches, and Michael Bunker announces. The order below follows the four posted parts.

evidence.note: Part one of the posting: Jobba the Butt's return promo, the card, the first four King of Christmas matches and the build-ups for the tag title match.
Part two: the Unified Tag Team Title match and the two King of Christmas semifinals.
Part three: Captain Midnight against Alex Adams, the King of Christmas final and the promos for the two title matches.
Part four: the North American Championship match, the World Heavyweight Championship ladder match, the Santa finish and the per-match credits.
